combining several gate results into one overall score or label

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Shared maturity framework header
sections.what: The opening comment says this file is the one shared source for the six maturity gates, their order and names, and how they combine into a five-level label. The server and the browser both use it.
sections.why: Likely reason: avoids two copies of the same rules drifting apart. Reason stated only in the header comment.
sections.watch_out: A change here affects both the server and the browser at once.

sections.name: MATURITY_GATE_KEYS, MaturityGateKey
sections.title: The six maturity gate keys
sections.what: Lists the six areas a project is judged on, in order: site control, permitting, financing, offtake, EPC contracts, and technology. Other code uses these names as fixed labels.
sections.why: The header calls them the six researched gates. The type is derived from this list so that misspelled gate names are caught by the compiler.
sections.watch_out: Order matters if screens show gates in list order. Adding a gate also requires updating the gate details further down the file.

sections.name: MaturityGateMeta
sections.title: Definition of one maturity gate
sections.what: Describes the shape of one maturity gate: a key, a full label, a short label, a plain description, and a list of search phrases. The research engine uses those phrases to look for evidence that the gate is cleared.
sections.why: The comment on the search phrases says they guide the research engine, so the phrases decide what evidence it looks for.
sections.watch_out: Editing a search phrase changes which evidence gets found, so results can shift even though no logic changed.

sections.name: MATURITY_GATES, GateStatus
sections.title: The six maturity gates and status options
sections.what: Lists the six gates a project must pass to show maturity: site control, permits, financing, offtake, EPC contracts and technology readiness. Each has a description and search phrases. It also defines the four possible states of a gate: cleared, in progress, not started and unknown.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the fixed order of the gates.
sections.watch_out: The roll-up logic assumes exactly six gates, so adding or removing one needs a matching change in the roll-up rule.

sections.name: gateStatusScore, MATURITY_TIERS, MaturityTier
sections.title: Scores for gate status and tier names
sections.what: Converts each gate state into a number from zero to one: cleared is one, in progress is one half, and everything else is zero. It also lists the five maturity tiers from concept up to bankable.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The roll-up rule in this file does not use the score, and the code does not say where it is used.
sections.watch_out: An unknown status and a not-started status both score zero, so an unrecognized status is treated the same as not started.

sections.name: DerivedMaturity
sections.title: Shape of a maturity tier and likelihood
sections.what: Describes the pair that holds a maturity tier name and a likelihood number. The values used in this file, such as 10, 50 and 100, suggest the likelihood is a percentage.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond keeping the tier and the likelihood together as one value.
sections.watch_out: The code does not check that the likelihood stays between zero and 100.

sections.name: DEFAULT_DERIVED_MATURITY
sections.title: Default maturity for unknown lifecycle stages
sections.what: The fallback for a project whose lifecycle stage is missing or unrecognized: a LOW tier with a likelihood of 50. The comment says this is the value bulk-loaded projects historically started with.
sections.why: The comment says it is the historic ingest default, which keeps the old behavior for unknown stages.
sections.watch_out: A misspelled stage name silently gets this fallback rather than an error.

sections.name: deriveMaturityFromLifecycle
sections.title: Maturity tier from project lifecycle stage
sections.what: Maps a project's lifecycle stage to a starting tier and likelihood, so bulk-loaded projects do not all start at the same low default. Operating and retired projects get the top tier, on-hold projects stay low, and cancelled projects drop to concept.
sections.why: The long comment explains the choices: retired projects were fully realized, on-hold projects rarely restart on schedule, and cancelled projects will not proceed.
sections.watch_out: This is only a starting guess. The comment says a real research result must never be overwritten, but this function does not protect it, so callers must check.

sections.name: RolledUpGate
sections.title: Pair of gate key and status
sections.what: A small record holding one gate's key and its current status. It is the input shape the tier roll-up expects.
sections.why: Keeps the input to the roll-up rule in a simple, known shape.

sections.name: rollupMaturityTier
sections.title: Tier roll-up from cleared gates
sections.what: Counts how many of the six gates are cleared and returns one tier: six gives bankable, four or more gives high, two or three gives medium, one gives low, and none gives concept. This is how the maturity label for a project is produced from its gate states.
sections.why: The comment says only fully cleared gates set the tier, and bankable needs all six.
sections.watch_out: The comment says in-progress gates count as half toward a weighted total, but this code ignores in-progress gates and calculates no weighted total. The financing check also has no effect, because both branches return the same tier.

summary: Holds the shared list of six maturity gates and, in parts not visible here, their labels and the roll-up to a five-level maturity label.
purpose: Makes the server and the browser agree on the same gate names, order, and maturity labels.
why: The file header says it is the single source of truth, so one place changes without breaking either side. Reason for the exact design not stated.
how: The file defines the six gate keys in order and derives a type from them. The rest of the file, which was not visible, defines gate descriptions, scoring, a derived maturity value, and a function that rolls gate results up into one tier.
inputs: The visible part takes no inputs. Later parts, which were not visible, take per-gate statuses.
outputs: A fixed list of gate keys and a type for them. Other functions, not visible here, produce a maturity tier.
risks: Reordering or renaming a gate changes what every screen shows. Only the header and gate key list were visible.
debug: If a gate is missing or misspelled, check the gate key list first. Then check the gate details and roll-up sections, which were not visible.
